guidance.one_liner: A company's own forecast of its future sales or profit.

consensus.one_liner: The average forecast of the analysts who follow a company.

eps.one_liner: Profit divided by the number of shares: your slice of profit per share.

gross margin.one_liner: The share of each sale left after paying to make the product.

operating margin.one_liner: What is left after also paying for research, sales and offices.

p/e.one_liner: Share price divided by yearly profit per share: years of profit you pay for.

gaap.one_liner: The official accounting rulebook; non-GAAP numbers leave some costs out.

non-gaap.one_liner: Adjusted numbers that leave some costs out and usually look better.

market cap.one_liner: Share price times number of shares: what the market says the company is worth.

backlog.one_liner: Orders signed but not yet delivered.

capex.one_liner: Money spent on long-lasting things like factories and machines.

etf.one_liner: A fund that trades on the exchange like a share and holds a basket of stocks.

beta.one_liner: How much a stock tends to move when the market moves 1%.

correlation.one_liner: How often two stocks move the same way on the same day, from -1 to +1.

drawdown.one_liner: A fall from a previous high.

moving average.one_liner: The average price over the last 50 or 200 days.

rsi.one_liner: Relative strength index; above 70 means a stock rose fast recently.

value at risk.one_liner: A loss exceeded only on the worst 1 day in 20, based on the past.

8-k.one_liner: A US filing reporting an important company event.

10-q.one_liner: The quarterly report a US company files.

10-k.one_liner: The annual report a US company files.

form 4.one_liner: A filing showing an insider traded shares.

form 144.one_liner: A notice that an insider plans to sell shares.

10b5-1.one_liner: A selling schedule an insider sets months ahead, so they do not pick the moment of each sale.

dilution.one_liner: New shares created, so each existing share owns a smaller slice.

buyback.one_liner: A company buying its own shares, so each remaining share owns more.

export controls.one_liner: Government rules about what may be sold to which countries.

arr.one_liner: The yearly value of all active subscriptions.

net new arr.one_liner: How much ARR grew during one quarter, after customers who left.

net revenue retention.one_liner: What last year's customers spend now vs last year.

free cash flow.one_liner: Cash left after paying the bills and investing in equipment.

gpu.one_liner: A chip that does many small calculations at once; suits AI.

hyperscaler.one_liner: The giant cloud companies that build the biggest data centers.

active electrical cable.one_liner: Copper cable with a chip at each end to strengthen the signal.

optical transceiver.one_liner: Plug-in module turning electrical signals into light and back.

market order.one_liner: An order to buy or sell right away at whatever the price is.

limit order.one_liner: An order to buy or sell only at a set price or better.

attribution.one_liner: How much of a move came from the market, the industry and the company itself.

z-score.one_liner: A move measured in the stock's usual swings.

capped call.one_liner: A hedge a company buys so convertible bonds create fewer new shares.

convertible bonds.one_liner: Loans to a company that can be swapped for shares if the price rises enough.

force majeure.one_liner: A contract clause excusing delays caused by events outside a party's control.

index fund.one_liner: A fund that copies an index and must buy stocks added to it.

shelf filing.one_liner: SEC permission to sell shares or debt later, without selling yet.

class action.one_liner: A lawsuit filed on behalf of many shareholders at once.

thesis breaker.one_liner: An event on your list that would challenge why you own a stock.

fractional share.one_liner: A piece of one share; earns the same percentage as a whole share, on fewer dollars.

at-the-market offering.one_liner: A company selling new shares a little at a time into the market through a broker.

selling overhang.one_liner: Steady selling that weighs on a price until it stops.

schedule 13g.one_liner: Short SEC form a passive holder of 5% or more files; 13D is the activist version.

index rebalancing.one_liner: Index funds buying and selling when a company joins or leaves their list, usually at the close.

treasury yield.one_liner: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow.

rate hike.one_liner: The central bank making borrowing more expensive to slow price rises.

conversion price.one_liner: The share price above which a convertible bond's lender gains by swapping it for shares.

presidential symposium.one_liner: The main session of a big medical conference, for the most important new trial results.

foundry.one_liner: A factory that makes chips designed by other companies.

anchor customer.one_liner: A big first customer whose orders make a new factory worth building.

settlement.one_liner: When shares and cash actually change hands; one business day after a US trade (T+1).

record date.one_liner: The day you must be on the company's books to get a dividend.

price target.one_liner: The price an analyst expects in about a year; an opinion, not a fact.

remaining performance obligations.one_liner: Signed contracts not yet billed: future revenue already agreed.

var.one_liner: A loss exceeded only on the worst 1 day in 20, based on past behaviour.

fiscal year.one_liner: A company's own accounting year, which need not match the calendar.

s&p 500.one_liner: An index of 500 large US companies; used here as 'the market'.

nasdaq-100.one_liner: A list of 100 large companies on the Nasdaq exchange that many funds copy.

52-week high.one_liner: The highest price a stock reached in the past year.

stop-loss.one_liner: A price set in advance to be alerted if a stock falls that far.

target price.one_liner: A price set in advance to be alerted if a stock rises that far.

phase 3.one_liner: The final, largest round of patient testing before a medicine can be approved.

insider.one_liner: A company's top managers, directors or 10% owners, who must report their trades.

source tiers.one_liner: Tier 1: company or regulator; tier 2: established newsrooms; tier 3: secondary sites to confirm.

thesis status.one_liner: Intact, Watch, Challenged or Broken: how today's evidence compares with your pillars and triggers.

present value.one_liner: What a future dollar is worth today; higher interest rates make far-off dollars worth less now.

profit-taking.one_liner: Selling a stock that has risen fast to lock in the gain; it can push a price down with no news.

ex-dividend date.one_liner: The first day a buyer no longer gets the next dividend; the price usually drops by about the dividend.

proxy statement.one_liner: The papers sent before the yearly shareholder meeting, listing what owners vote on.

form 3.one_liner: The first report a new insider files, listing the shares they already own.

tax withholding (code f).one_liner: Shares a company keeps back to pay an employee's tax when stock awards vest; not a market sale.

10b5-1 plan.one_liner: A selling schedule an insider sets months ahead, so they do not pick the moment of each sale.

expense ratio.one_liner: A fund's yearly fee as a share of your money; QQQM's 0.15% is 15 cents per $100.

look-through.one_liner: Counting what is inside a fund, so you see overlap with stocks you already own.

optical circuit switch.one_liner: A switch that redirects light between fibres with tiny mirrors, like a railway switch for light.

hybrid bonding.one_liner: Joining stacked chips directly, copper to copper, used for AI memory.

behind-the-meter.one_liner: A power plant on the customer's own site, on their side of the electricity meter.

convertible preferred shares.one_liner: Special shares that can turn into ordinary shares later, raising the share count.

convertible bond.one_liner: A loan the lender can swap for shares above a set price.

headline sensitivity.one_liner: A stock jumping on theme news before anyone checks whether its sales would change.

cpu.one_liner: The general-purpose chip that runs a computer's software and hands out work.

endpoint.one_liner: Any laptop, server or phone on a company network that must be protected.

firewall.one_liner: A device or program that decides which network traffic may enter or leave.

overweight rating.one_liner: An analyst's view that a stock will beat the market; an opinion, not a fact.

phase 3 trial.one_liner: The last and largest round of testing in patients before a drug can be approved.

priced in.one_liner: Already reflected in the price because investors expected it.

annualized revenue.one_liner: Today's sales pace stretched to a full year; a pace, not a year of reported sales.

run rate.one_liner: Today's sales pace stretched to a full quarter or year; a pace, not reported sales.

warrant.one_liner: A right to buy shares at a fixed price, often very low; if used, new shares dilute existing owners.

personalised cancer vaccine.one_liner: A vaccine made for one patient from their tumour's genes, teaching the immune system to attack it.

social engineering.one_liner: Tricking a person into handing over a password instead of breaking the software.

sold out.one_liner: Customers have reserved everything a factory can make for a period: predictable sales, firmer prices.

pricing power.one_liner: A seller's ability to keep or raise prices without losing customers.

book-to-burn.one_liner: New work signed divided by work completed; above 1 means future work is piling up.

monthly revenue.one_liner: Sales published every month (like TSMC's), an early look before quarterly results.

preliminary results.one_liner: Early, rounded figures published before the full quarterly report.

employee stock purchase plan.one_liner: A company program that buys shares for staff on preset terms; routine, not a signal.

grat.one_liner: A family trust used to pass shares to relatives; moving shares in is a gift, not a sale.

gift (code g).one_liner: An insider gives shares away (often to a trust or charity); no money changes hands.

foundation (charitable).one_liner: A charity that receives donated shares; if an executive controls it, its sales are reported like an insider's.

interposer.one_liner: A thin silicon base on which an AI chip and its memory sit side by side, wired together.

cowos.one_liner: TSMC's way of packaging an AI chip and its memory together on an interposer.

relative weakness.one_liner: A stock doing worse than its own industry even on good days.

momentum.one_liner: Buying because a stock has been rising; can push prices beyond what facts justify.

50-day average.one_liner: Average closing price of the last 50 trading days; breaks below it can trigger trend-following selling.

compressed natural gas.one_liner: Gas squeezed into tanks and trucked where no pipeline exists; works but costs more.

bookings.one_liner: Value of new orders signed in a period; ASML stopped publishing them quarterly in 2026.

laser chip.one_liner: The tiny laser in an optical module that turns electrical signals into light.

fab.one_liner: A chip factory (fabrication plant); a new one takes years to build.

ocp.one_liner: Open Compute Project Global Summit: a yearly data-center hardware conference.

esmo.one_liner: European Society for Medical Oncology; its congress is a main stage for cancer-trial results.

nih.one_liner: National Institutes of Health, the US government's medical research agency.

public-private partnership.one_liner: A project run jointly by a government agency and companies.

trading volume.one_liner: How many shares changed hands in a day; heavy volume means many investors acted at once.

analyst labels.one_liner: Ratings like Buy, Outperform, Neutral or Sell: one analyst's opinion of how a stock will do.

gigawatt.one_liner: A billion watts; about the output of a large power plant.

hbm.one_liner: High-bandwidth memory: stacked memory chips that feed AI processors data very fast.

dram.one_liner: The main working memory in computers and servers.

mrna.one_liner: Genetic instructions that tell cells to make a specific protein; the basis of Moderna's vaccines.

co-packaged optics.one_liner: Putting the optical (light) parts right next to the chip instead of in a separate plug-in module.

dividend.one_liner: Cash a company pays its owners, usually every quarter.

fed.one_liner: The Federal Reserve, the US central bank that sets short-term interest rates.
